purpose: Response-free known-truth intervention experiment to causally separate three representation defects observed in Tampa without reopening any ecological endpoint.

design.split: fixed first 60 nodes train, last 20 nodes heldout; first 10 contexts fitting, last 6 contexts scoring

known_truth.clean_layer_b: ten fixed nonlinear functions of the current dynamic_latent_state, x, y and context_phase; generated identically for train and heldout rows
known_truth.static_reuse_intervention: replace each node's current Layer-B rows by its mean Layer-B vector over fitting contexts, then reuse that vector for every context
known_truth.generator_shift_intervention: training Layer-B uses the selected representation unchanged; heldout Layer-B applies fixed affine/sign transform [z0,z1,...] -> [-z0, z1+1.5, -z2, z3+1.0, z4, -z5, z6+0.75, z7, -z8, z9+0.5]
known_truth.single_source_intervention: prediction-facing Layer-B receives a fixed node-label-dependent sign mask determined by whether the synthetic node label is lexicographically below N040; clean condition uses source-symmetric identity mask

estimands.primary: paired cell log-loss difference relative to the clean 000 cell within the same replicate
estimands.main_effect_generator_shift: mean over matched cells of loss(factor G=1)-loss(G=0)
estimands.main_effect_static_reuse: mean over matched cells of loss(S=1)-loss(S=0)
estimands.main_effect_single_source: mean over matched cells of loss(A=1)-loss(A=0)
estimands.baseline_reference: baseline RF log loss is reported but does not define mechanism success

forbidden_interpretations: Synthetic effect magnitudes estimate how much each mechanism caused Tampa's observed +0.1010287 log-loss delta
Passing this benchmark proves Layer-B v2 improves prediction in real ecological systems
This benchmark authorizes a Tampa rerun or a fourth fresh EOG-WF endpoint
The benchmark changes the favorable/favorable/adverse empirical synthesis
